findings.quote: Team Settings → Git → "Connect" GitHub → install the Vercel GitHub App on the `RadioDinner` account → "Only select repositories" → `ChurchAppCLD`.
findings.problem: Vercel team settings have no Git tab; the Vercel GitHub App is normally installed from the 'Add New → Project → Import Git Repository' flow, which item 3.4 forbids ('Do not import a project yet'). The founder cannot complete 3.3 as written and either stalls or imports the project two steps early.
findings.fix: Replace item 3.3 with: 'Install the Vercel GitHub App without importing: github.com/apps/vercel → Configure → choose the `RadioDinner` account → "Only select repositories" → `ChurchAppCLD` → Save. (Alternative: Vercel → Add New… → Project → "Continue with GitHub" → "Adjust GitHub App Permissions" and stop before clicking Import.) Check: Vercel → Add New… → Project lists `ChurchAppCLD` under Import Git Repository — do not click Import.'

findings.quote: Be on Pro before step 2.5: the repo ships `apps/web/vercel.json` with a `*/5 * * * *` cron
findings.problem: Item 3.2 tells the founder to create the team on Pro now, the sentence after it says Pro is only needed before 2.5, notes say 'needed before 2.5, not today', and done_when 3 requires 'a team on the Pro plan exists'. Two readings, two outcomes (pay from today or not).
findings.fix: Pick one and align all four places. Recommended: item 3.2 = 'Create Team → name `Anacast` → plan Hobby (free) for now; upgrade to Pro (Team Settings → Billing → Upgrade) at the start of step 2.5, before the first import — the `*/5` cron is rejected on Hobby and Hobby forbids commercial use.' done_when 3 = 'a Vercel team named Anacast exists, the Vercel GitHub App has access to ChurchAppCLD, no project imported; HANDOFF notes "upgrade to Pro at 2.5"'. Tell the reviser of G6 2.5 to add the upgrade as its first item.

findings.quote: turn on two-factor authentication on every account — these accounts will hold church members' personal data.
findings.problem: 2FA is a done_when item (8) but appears only in the preamble; no numbered sub-item says where the switch is, so it is the item most likely to be skipped.
findings.fix: Add a sub-item to each account block: GitHub 'Settings → Password and authentication → Two-factor authentication → Enable'; Supabase 'Account (avatar) → Account Settings → Security → Multi-factor authentication → Add'; Vercel 'Account Settings → Authentication → Two-Factor Authentication'; Stripe 'Settings → Team and security → Your profile → Two-step authentication'. Keep done_when 8.

findings.problem: Step 4.1's `app.config.ts` needs the Expo account/username for the `owner` field and 4.5's `eas init` links the project to that account; the checklist never tells the founder to record which username was chosen, and the helper prompt's Inputs have no line for it.
findings.fix: Item 5: append 'Record the Expo username in HANDOFF.md (Environment status → Accounts) — step 4.1 uses it as `owner` in `app.config.ts`.' Helper prompt Inputs: add '- Expo username: <value | deferred to 4.5>' and write it in Build 1.

findings.quote: - `git diff HANDOFF.md` shows only the additions above and contains no secret.
findings.problem: 'Contains no secret' is a judgement, not a check; the helper also edits docs/TODO.md and the session folder, so 'only the additions above' is false as stated.
findings.fix: Replace Verify with: '- `git status --short` lists only `HANDOFF.md`, `docs/TODO.md` and the current `Session log/NNN_*/` folder. - `git diff -- HANDOFF.md docs/TODO.md | grep -Ei "sk_(live|test)_|sb_(secret|publishable)_|eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}|@[a-z0-9-]+\.(com|org|net)"` prints nothing (the literal placeholder `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>` is fine).'

findings.problem: Prettier reformats markdown tables and lists, and the repo already holds hand-written docs with wide tables (docs/PLAN.md, docs/DESIGN.md, HANDOFF.md, CLAUDE.md, new_session_instructions.md). `prettier --check .` fails on them; one agent will run `prettier --write` over the design docs (a huge, meaningless diff to files other steps quote by line) and another will drop the check — incompatible results.
findings.fix: In Build item 5 add to `.prettierignore`: `docs/PLAN.md`, `docs/DESIGN.md`, `HANDOFF.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `new_session_instructions.md`, `docs/TODO.md` (hand-maintained; never reformat), and set `"proseWrap": "preserve"` in `.prettierrc`. Add to Constraints: 'Never run `prettier --write` on the pre-existing docs.' Add to Build item 15: 'run `pnpm format` once (it touches only files you created) before `pnpm format:check`.' Keep the Verify bullet.

findings.quote: DB re-runnability + RLS tests (guard `scripts/db/test.sh`; add a `postgres:16` service container; step 1.2 owns what the scripts do in CI)
findings.problem: The agent must still write a `run:` body and the connection env for this step, and G2's 1.2 already fixes the contract (service `postgres:16`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres`, health check, `PG_SUPER_URL=postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/postgres`, then the standing sequence). Left open, 1.1 invents a different variable name or command list and 1.2 has to rewrite the job.
findings.fix: Replace the parenthetical with the exact contents: 'job-level `services: postgres: { image: postgres:16, env: { POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres }, ports: ["5432:5432"], options: --health-cmd pg_isready --health-interval 10s --health-timeout 5s --health-retries 5 }`; step `if: hashFiles(\'scripts/db/test.sh\') != \'\'`, `env: { PG_SUPER_URL: postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/postgres }`, `run: bash scripts/db/local-up.sh && bash scripts/db/apply-migrations.sh && bash scripts/db/apply-migrations.sh && bash scripts/db/check-rerunnable.sh && bash scripts/db/test.sh`. Step 1.2 makes `local-up.sh` honour `PG_SUPER_URL`; do not change the variable name.'

findings.quote: types drift (guard `packages/db/src/database.types.ts`; run `bash scripts/db/gen-types.sh` then `git diff --exit-code packages/db/src/database.types.ts`)
findings.problem: `gen-types.sh` reads `DATABASE_URL`, but GitHub Actions does not carry a variable exported by an earlier step's shell into later steps, so the drift step as written has no database URL and fails as soon as its guard switches on (step 1.5). Agents will resolve this differently ($GITHUB_ENV, hard-coded URL, re-running local-up).
findings.fix: Write the step fully: place it immediately after the DB step, with `env: { DATABASE_URL: postgresql://churchapp_owner:churchapp@localhost:5432/churchapp?sslmode=disable }` (the URL 1.2 derives in CI) and `run: bash scripts/db/gen-types.sh && git diff --exit-code packages/db/src/database.types.ts`. Note in the YAML comment that 1.5 may adjust the command but not the variable name.

findings.quote: - `pnpm ls -r --depth -1` → exactly five workspace packages: `@church/domain`, `@church/db`, `@church/supabase-client`, `@church/eslint-config`, `@church/tsconfig`; nothing under `apps/`.
findings.problem: `pnpm ls -r --depth -1` also prints the root project `churchappcld`, so the literal 'exactly five' fails and the agent second-guesses the scaffold.
findings.fix: Write: '→ the root `churchappcld` plus exactly five workspace packages: …; nothing under `apps/`.' (Same wording in done_when 3.)

findings.quote: - After the push: the `ci` workflow run on GitHub Actions completes (green; the job is non-blocking either way).
findings.problem: No command is given and the agent may not be able to open github.com; it also depends on Actions being enabled (0.1 item 1.3), which contradicts the Inputs line 'Step 0.1 … may or may not be done; nothing here depends on it.'
findings.fix: Replace with: '- After the push: `gh run list --workflow ci --limit 1` shows the run; `gh run watch <id> --exit-status` ends 0 (if `gh` is not authenticated, ask me to confirm from the Actions tab). This needs GitHub Actions enabled (step 0.1 item 1.3); if the run never starts, say so in the final message instead of retrying.' Change the Inputs line to 'Step 0.1 may or may not be done; only the final CI-run check needs it.'

findings.problem: The packages reach `tooling/tsconfig` through a pnpm symlink and then a relative `../../tsconfig.base.json`; it works because tsc realpaths package `extends`, but nothing in Verify proves the root options actually arrive in the packages, and a broken chain still typechecks green (looser options).
findings.fix: Add to Verify: '- `pnpm --filter @church/domain exec tsc -p tsconfig.json --showConfig | grep -E "noUncheckedIndexedAccess|verbatimModuleSyntax"` prints both options set to true (proves the `@church/tsconfig` → `tsconfig.base.json` chain resolves through the symlink).'

findings.problem: The reverted scaffold imported `eslint-config-expo/flat.js`; whether the bare `/flat` subpath resolves depends on the package's exports map, and the Verify bullet imports `@church/eslint-config/expo`, so a wrong specifier fails the step for an avoidable reason.
findings.fix: Write: '`expo.js` (base + the flat config from `eslint-config-expo` — import `eslint-config-expo/flat`; if that subpath is not exported, use `eslint-config-expo/flat.js`, whichever `node -e "import(\'eslint-config-expo/flat\')"` resolves).'
